question: Under this frozen configuration, does the deterministic candidate generator retrieve the labelled documents?
question_scope_note: Deliberately narrower than 'is the retriever the problem?', which earlier drafts used. This measures PgVectorStore.hybrid_search alone. Production retrieval also rewrites the query and reranks, so a good score here does NOT clear the production retrieval path, and a bad one does not by itself indict it. Claims about production retrieval need the pipeline evaluation, which is ORQ-27's.

golden_set.note: Grade 0 is implicit for unjudged source_paths and never written. Judged paths per query are 1 or 2, so the >= 1 relevance rule admits every judgment; the graded scale is carried for future graded metrics, not used by the metrics registered below.

instrument.measures: the deterministic candidate generator, not RetrievalPipeline

embedding.rationale: Same call ORQ-22 used (build_dataset.py:52-57), so the ceiling numbers are directly comparable. Changing the embedding model would make this run measure something else; that swap is deferred and is itself a candidate for a later run of this harness.

instrument.determinism_requires: the ORDER BY tiebreakers of ORQ-26 Task 0; before that commit hybrid_search had no stable ordering under RRF score ties

corpus.rationale: ORQ-26 both edits a labelled document (app/core/providers/pgvector_store.py, judged grade 2 by q045/q046 and grade 1 by q015/q016) and adds new documents under docs/adr/ that ingestion would pick up. Measuring HEAD would let this ORQ's own text raise the term frequency of a labelled document in the terms of the query that judges it, and let an unlabelled ADR compete for top-k against labelled documents. Pinning the corpus to the branch merge-base removes both effects by construction rather than by careful wording.

repinning_policy.baseline_runs: Retain d849f08 permanently. These are comparable to each other and to nothing else; that is their whole purpose.
repinning_policy.production_relevance_runs: Must re-pin to a reviewed commit rather than inherit this one. Each re-pin records source commit, ingestion config, document and chunk counts, and the golden-set hash, and re-runs the leakage and contamination checks against the new corpus.
repinning_policy.inheritance: ORQ-27 and ORQ-28 do NOT inherit this pin by default. A pinned corpus drifts further from production with every ORQ, so inheriting it silently would turn a one-time contamination control into a permanently stale baseline presented as current evidence.
repinning_policy.note: The corpus manifest is written by app.scripts.ingest_corpus and read by the runner, which refuses to execute without it. It is an honest declaration of what the ingesting process saw, not a proof: a later hand-edit of the database would not invalidate it. Proving the correspondence would mean recomputing every content_hash from the pinned worktree at run time.

metrics.scored_unit: distinct source_path, resolved from the retrieved document_id by a post-query lookup
metrics.window: top-k chunks, collapsed to distinct source_path after retrieval
metrics.k_rationale: 20 is the pool RetrievalPipeline would consume; 30 matches ORQ-22's ceiling measurement.
metrics.document_rank: dense - position in the collapsed distinct-source_path list, not the first-occurrence chunk rank
metrics.relevance_note: These are binary-relevance metrics, not graded ones. Every judgment in the golden set is grade 1 or 2, so >= 1 admits all of them and the grade scale carries no discriminating power here. Per-query recall therefore takes only the values 0, 0.5 and 1. The grade scale must not be cited as evidence of finer discrimination than that. A graded metric, or a separate primary-relevance (grade 2 only) analysis, would need its own registration before being run.

decision_rule.statement: The CANDIDATE GENERATOR baseline is judged inadequate if EITHER aggregate recall@10 falls below recall_at_10_floor, OR (aggregate recall@20 - aggregate recall@10) exceeds recall_gap_margin. The verdict is about hybrid_search under this frozen configuration and this pinned corpus. It is not a verdict on 'the retriever' or on production retrieval, which also rewrites and reranks.
decision_rule.gap_clause_means: Candidate-pool depth sensitivity: retrieving 20 chunks recovers substantially more labelled documents than retrieving 10.
decision_rule.gap_clause_does_not_mean_ranking_efficie: The gap must NOT be read as 'the documents were in the pool but ranked too low'. LIMIT :top_k sits inside each CTE, so k=10 and k=20 build different pre-fusion pools; the comparison measures sensitivity to pool depth, not ranking quality within a fixed pool.
decision_rule.thresholds_note: Set and committed before any run, per the pre-registration discipline. recall_at_10_floor = 0.65: ORQ-22's frozen dataset gives an aggregate recall@10 of 0.7167 over the same 60 queries; 0.65 allows roughly a 10% relative margin for corpus drift accumulated across ORQ-23/24/25. recall_gap_margin = 0.12: the same prior gives a recall@20 - recall@10 gap of 0.0750; 0.12 is a factor of ~1.6 above it, covering the different pre-fusion pool composition at k=10 versus k=20. Both priors were computed from experiments/reranking/dataset.jsonl, which predates this ORQ entirely, so they calibrate the rule without previewing the run.

leakage_assertion.claim: No golden-set query string occurs in the ingested text of the measured corpus.
leakage_assertion.asserted_against: a tenant-scoped chunks query, not the filesystem
leakage_assertion.rationale: The vectors were written at an earlier commit, so a later rephrasing on disk would hide a leak that the corpus still carries.

reporting.note: Re-registration requires a new commit. Every runs row carries this file's sha256 and the commit that introduced it. Runs under earlier registration hashes are reported alongside, never replaced.

enforcement_status.note: experiments/evaluation/run_evaluation.py implements the guards. It refuses to run on a modified or uncommitted registration.json, on null thresholds, on a missing approval signature, on a golden-set hash mismatch, on a missing corpus manifest, on a manifest whose commit differs from the pinned one, and on any golden-set query found in the ingested corpus.
enforced_today: golden_set.sha256 matches at run time and via build_golden_set.py --check
corpus manifest present and matching the pinned commit
no golden-set query text in the measured corpus
